_comment: Custody manifest (example). Copy, edit, and point CUSTODY_MANIFEST at it.
Declares what this collection considers ITS OWN, so custody-audit can ask four questions and
nothing more: is each artifact tracked or deliberately ignored with a stated disposition; is the
encrypted counterpart current and committed; is HEAD on a declared remote; is this the canonical
working copy. Every other engine validates CONTENT and passes whether or not that content has
ever been committed, pushed or backed up.
JSON rather than YAML only because it is read by tooling more often than by people. Comments
live in _comment keys, which the engine ignores.

artifacts._comment: The ordinary case. A finding here means git does not carry something you believe it does.
Deliberately disposable. Declaring it is what distinguishes 'ignored on purpose' from the silent gap: untracked-and-unignored, which nothing else reports.

_comment: The interesting row. 'Sensitive file gitignored, sanitised example committed beside it' is
CORRECT practice that nothing enforces, and the example sitting next to the gap is exactly
what makes a missing counterpart invisible.
Three ways this fails, all reported: no counterpart at all; a counterpart OLDER than the file
it backs up, which is not a backup; a counterpart that exists and was never committed, which
protects against nothing beyond this disk.

_comment_remotes: ABSENT means assume origin. An explicitly EMPTY list means no remote is declared and the
question is not asked. Those are different states and collapsing them made a manifest that
deliberately declares no remote report a missing one.
_comment_canonical: Where this collection is supposed to live. The marker travels WITH a copy, which is what lets a
copy report that it is one: a rollback copy is complete, valid, passes every content check, and
is indistinguishable from the original in an editor. Work done in it commits cleanly and is
stranded. Omit the key entirely if you keep only one copy.

receipts.name: nightly-backup
receipts._comment: Scheduled work reports by WRITING a receipt; this engine checks its freshness and never inspects systemd, cron or Task Scheduler. Three platforms, three failure modes, no determinism. It also avoids a job that reports failed every night while the half that matters succeeds, since a permanently red signal is indistinguishable from a real one.
